title: Investigating strength training exercise prior to surgery in patients with gullet and stomach cancer
official: STEPTOE: Strengthening exercise prehabilitation during treatment of oesophagogastric cancer
summary:
Background and study aims
People dealing with a new cancer diagnosis and treatment often experience feelings of weakness, exhaustion, fatigue and low wellbeing. To help them to cope, medical doctors and exercise professionals designed a new exercise therapy called “prehabilitation” giving patients the chance to exercise in safe, supervised settings to boost fitness and wellbeing ahead of surgery and to improve recovery from surgery. This has been well adopted and developed in Greater Manchester and is called “Prehab4cancer”. Prehab4cancer has treated over 4000 patients in Greater Manchester.
The surgical team in Salford Royal (the centre for gullet and stomach cancer in Manchester) have noticed that over half of our patients with Oesophageal and Gastric cancers still develop a serious muscle disease called sarcopenia causing muscle wasting, weakness and poor physical function (e.g. slow walking speeds, difficulty getting up from sitting down). Sarcopenia increases risk of poor surgery outcomes and slower recovery. Our research will trial a different form of exercise - called resistance exercise - to prevent sarcopenia from occurring during chemotherapy treatment. We think that it will work by increasing muscular strength, muscle mass and physical fitness which make the body more tolerant and able to cope with cancer treatments. 

Who can participate?
Patients with gullet or stomach cancer having chemotherapy prior to surgery.

What does the study involve?
In this randomised, controlled study, 100 patients will be assessed. 50 patients will complete resistance exercise 2-times per week for 60minues with supervision of an exercise physiologist, throughout chemotherapy and ahead of surgery, and their muscle health and physical function will be compared with 50 patients who complete the standard Prehab4Cancer exercises. The standard exercise is based on an exercise bike. All patients enrolled in the trial will be asked to complete a further 60minutes exercise at home every week with guidance from the exercise physiologist. Clinical assessments of strength, muscle mass, physical function and cell biology will be used to determine whether the newer form of resistance exercises can prevent sarcopenia by keeping patients stronger and better able to complete daily activities independently. We will assess participants at baseline, after their chemotherapy ends and just prior to surgery. 

What are the possible benefits and risks of participating?
Participants in the study will benefit from tailored, supervised exercise sessions with regular assessments to see progress. All patients having this treatment in Greater Manchester have prehab and there are no added risks of this exercise. Having supervised exercise sessions means some participants may have to travel further than they usually would for their prehab as well as the travel associated with attending the university for assessments. We do have funding for some travel reimbursement.
The findings of our research will be used for patient benefit by informing the design of future exercise “prehabilitation” therapies and preparing practical tools and guidelines for other prehab providers to deliver improved patient outcomes. 

Where is the study run from?
Northern Care Alliance NHS Foundation Trust (UK)

When is the study starting and how long is it expected to run for?
June 2026 to March 2029

Who is funding the study?
North West Cancer Research (UK)

Who is the main contact?
Jennifer Redfern – the trial manager and PhD student Jennifer.redfern2@nca.nhs.uk

interventions.name:
This study is a single centre, pilot, randomised control trial. Eligible patients from Salford Royal Hospital will be consulted and informed about the trial and if they consent will be randomised to either the control group or the intervention group. 
The randomisation will be independent, concealed

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1.	18 years old or older with locally advanced oesophageal, gastric or junctional adenocarcinoma (T2 N1 or above on initial composite staging) 
2.	Curative treatment pathway with neoadjuvant chemotherapy followed by surgery 
3.	Oesophagectomy by any approach including trial dissections or abandoned oesophagectomy. Gastrectomy by any approach including trial dissections or abandoned surgery.
4.	WHO performance status </= 2
Exclusion criteria:
1.	Squamous cell carcinoma 
2.	Palliative treatment pathway or development of unresectable disease during neoadjuvant treatment. 
3.	Treatment for recurrent oesophageal cancer or salvage treatment. 
4.	Synchronous malignancy elsewhere 
5.	Medically deemed unable to partake in resistance training program or study assessments due to significant musculoskeletal or mobility comorbidity. 
6.	Established neuromuscular diagnosis (inflammatory myopathy, idiopathic myositis) 
7.	Pregnancy 
8.	Unable to consent
